title: Stochastic sliding-window benchmark: annotated summary
body:
Purpose
---
Quick working summary of the sliding-window policy experiments we ran in June 2028. This doc compares:
  - Fixed-window allocation (baseline - 50 ms slot cadence)
  - Classic sliding-window (deterministic overlap windowing used in prior experiments)
  - Stochastic sliding-window (randomized start offsets + adaptive decay) — candidate policy for runtime rollout

Scope and goals
- Measure latency tail improvements vs baseline and associated unit-cost delta for typical chat-like workloads (short prompt + multi-turn continuation).
- Focus on sessionized traffic shape (bursty, median-turn 12 tokens, tail-turn 200 tokens) not bulk inference.
- Determine if stochastic windowing reduces tail p99 without materially increasing per-token cost.

Test harness and environment
- Cluster: 8x A100s (48GB) equivalent nodes; experiments run on a dedicated sandbox cluster to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Model: open-llm-xxl-16k (approx 22B) — representative of high-memory inference.
- Workload: 6 traffic profiles synthesized from production traces (cohort A-F). Each profile ran for 2h steady-state + 20% synthetic spikes.
- Concurrency: scaled from 50 -> 250 parallel sessions (step every 15min).
- Metrics captured: p50,p90,p95,p99 latency (ms) per-response, tokens/sec (aggregate), slot utilization (%), amortized cost per 1000 tokens (USD) using internal cost model (GPU-minute + amortized infra).
- Repeats: 3 independent runs for each policy; we report median across runs.

Raw numbers (median across runs)
(Values are per-response latency in ms; cost is amortized USD per 1k tokens)

Policy            | p50  | p90  | p95  | p99  | tokens/sec | slot util | $/1k tokens
------------------|------|------|------|------|------------|----------:|----------
Fixed-window      | 42   | 180  | 280  | 640  | 940        | 62%       | 4.82
Classic-sliding   | 40   | 150  | 220  | 520  | 1010       | 69%       | 4.95
Stochastic-slide  | 36   | 130  | 185  | 340  | 1075       | 71%       | 5.08

Notes on the table:
- Fixed-window baseline used conservative 50ms cadence that aligns with legacy job slot windows. High p99 due to contention spikes aligning across sessions.
- Classic sliding reduces alignment but still sees correlated microbursts that inflate p99.
- Stochastic sliding applied per-session random offsets (uniform(0,window)) and an adaptive decay where hot sessions shorten their effective window; this breaks global alignment and improves tail.

Simple ascii trend visualization (p99 latency across increasing concurrency)
Concurrency -> 50,100,150,200,250
Fixed-window p99 -> 180, 290, 360, 480, 640
Classic-slide p99 -> 160, 240, 310, 410, 520
Stochastic p99 -> 120, 180, 230, 280, 340

Interpretation
- Tail improvements: stochastic sliding delivered ~47% reduction in p99 at 250 concurrency vs fixed-window, and ~35% vs classic sliding.
- Median/90: consistent small improvements (p50 ~14% lower than fixed).
- Throughput & utilization: tokens/sec improved modestly (~14% over baseline), slot utilization improved ~9 percentage points vs fixed-window.
- Cost: amortized $/1k tokens increased by ~5% relative to fixed-window. The extra cost comes from slightly higher utilization (more active slots) and more frequent short-lived prefetch actions.

Why cost went up but tokens/sec also improved
- Stochastic offsets reduce synchrony but cause some duplicate prefetch attempts (trades prefetch redundancy for lower tail), and the adaptive decay shortens window for hot sessions which partially mitigates redundant work. Net effect: slightly higher absolute spend per token, but much lower tail latency.

SLO impact (hypothetical pricing tiers)
- For consumer-tier (p95 target 300ms): all three policies meet the target at concurrency <= 200, but fixed-window breaches p95 at 150+ on some cohorts. Stochastic-slide gives comfortable headroom.
- For enterprise-tier (p99 target 500ms): stochastic-slide is the only policy that stays comfortably below at 250 concurrency for the tested cohorts. Classic sliding approaches the threshold.

Operational considerations
- Complexity: stochastic policy requires per-session RNG seeds persisted for reproducible traces, and a decay controller to observe per-session "hotness". Implementation complexity is moderate but contained to runtime placement logic.
- Observability: need to add per-session window-latency heatmaps and a small counter for prefetch duplication events. Suggested dashboard PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pulls/302
- Rollout strategy: start with 10% traffic on dedicated capacity pool, monitor p99 and prefetch-dupe rate for 48h, then 30%, then 100%. Canary gating: prefetch-dupe < 8% and p99 reduction > 25% vs baseline.

Open questions / TODOs
- Measure impact on cheaper quantized variants (qa-8bit) — we used full float runs. Probable that cost delta shrinks for compact models.
- Assess behavior for long-turn sessions (>2000 tokens) — current workload focuses on short/medium. Edge case: stochastic offsets could shift KV cache eviction behavior; need a specific stress test.
- Tune adaptive decay parameters (decay-rate, hotness threshold) — current run used decay-rate=0.6 (empirical). Suggest sweep: [0.4,0.6,0.8].
- Investigate hybrid: deterministic small jitter + stochastic large offsets (might hit sweet spot of lower duplication).

Method details (reproducibility)
- Harness config: experiments/configs/windowing/stochastic/2028-06-12.yaml (see linked PR).
- Ingest trace scripts: tools/trace_pipeline/replay_cohorts.py --cohort A-F
- Cost model: internal/cost/compute_cost_v2 (GPU-minute + infra amortization). Approx calibration: $/GPU-min = 0.85; infra overhead = 28%
- Raw raw logs: s3://bench-results/2028-06-windowing/stochastic/ (privileged access)

Quick recommendation (for PM/infra planning)
- Short term: pilot stochastic-slide in the console runtime on a dedicated internal pool (10% traffic) and collect production signals. Expect ~30–45% p99 gain for modest ~5–7% increased unit spend for medium-turn chat workloads.
- Medium term: run parameter sweep for decay-rate and jitter distribution, add dashboards for dupe-prefetch and per-session window metrics.

Notes to self (work-in-progress style)
- Ethan: can you drop the p99-by-cohort plots into the confluence page? I left the notebook in the PR.
- Priya: want your take on rollout gating thresholds — current numbers are conservative.
- Jonas: double-check the cost calibration vs billing.csv for May (I think our infra delta might be slightly high).

References and provenance

- Slack thread: #runtime-windowing (thread ts: 17183291)
- Jira: JIRA-INF-4523 (epic for windowing strategies)

End of summary — this is intentionally terse; expand any section on request.
